claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar-colony microstructure.
The untreated alloy exhibits limited room-temperature ductility and brittleness.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause localized stress concentrations in the untreated alloy.
Cold rolling followed by controlled annealing can transform the lamellar colonies into an ultrafine duplex microstructure.
The resulting ultrafine duplex microstructure will have finer phase distributions and refined internal boundaries.
Reducing the size and spacing of internal boundaries will decrease the tendency for dislocation pile-ups.
Decreased dislocation pile-ups will reduce local stress concentrations.
The refined duplex microstructure will improve strain accommodation.
Reduced stress concentration and improved strain accommodation will delay microcrack nucleation.
Thermomechanical processing will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
Thermomechanical processing will maintain or increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The processed alloy will exhibit more uniform plastic deformation and a reduced incidence of microcracking.
The proposed benefits apply during room-temperature tensile loading and depend on achieving a uniformly refined duplex microstructure.
